name: Random Search
tagline: Greedy uniform-noise random search inside the L_inf ball: at each step accept a noise sample if it lowers the true-class logit.
pseudocode:
1. Initialize $x_{\text{adv}} = x$; query the true-class score $b = f(x_{\text{adv}})_y$
2. for $t = 1 \ldots \min(n_q, 64)$ do
3.   Sample $\delta_t \sim \mathrm{Unif}(-\epsilon/2, \epsilon/2)^d$
4.   $x' = \mathrm{clip}_{[0,1]}(x + \mathrm{clip}_{[-\epsilon,\epsilon]}(x_{\text{adv}} + \delta_t - x))$
5.   Query $s' = f(x')_y$; if $s' < b$ accept: $x_{\text{adv}} \leftarrow x',\, b \leftarrow s'$
6. end for
7. Return clipped $(x + \mathrm{clip}_{[-\epsilon,\epsilon]}(x_{\text{adv}} - x))$
diff_from_baseline: Andriushchenko & Hein 2019, Sect. 5 random-search baseline (and many earlier random-baselines). Greedy elementwise-uniform random noise inside the $L_\infty$ ball with score-only acceptance; weakest reasonable score-based attack and strong sanity check.

name: SPSA
tagline: Simultaneous Perturbation Stochastic Approximation: Bernoulli +/-1 finite-difference gradient estimates with PGD-style sign updates.
pseudocode:
1. Wrap with torchattacks.SPSA: $\delta = 0.01,\, \eta = 0.01,\, n_{\text{sample}} = 128,\, n_{\text{iter}} = \lfloor n_q / (2 n_{\text{sample}})\rfloor$
2. for $t = 1 \ldots n_{\text{iter}}$ do
3.   Sample $u_i \sim \mathrm{Unif}\{-1,+1\}^d$ for $i = 1\ldots n_{\text{sample}}$
4.   Estimate $\hat g \approx \frac{1}{n_{\text{sample}}}\sum_i \frac{L(x+\delta u_i, y) - L(x-\delta u_i, y)}{2\delta}\, u_i$
5.   $x \leftarrow x + \eta \cdot \mathrm{sign}(\hat g)$ then project to $[x_0 - \epsilon, x_0 + \epsilon] \cap [0,1]$
6. end for; return clipped $x_{\text{adv}}$
diff_from_baseline: Uesato et al. 2018 ("Adversarial Risk and the Dangers of Evaluating Against Weak Attacks"); originally Spall 1992. Score-based PGD-equivalent attack using SPSA's Bernoulli +/-1 finite-difference gradient estimator; standard strong baseline against gradient-masking defenses.

name: Square Attack
tagline: Score-based black-box attack that flips sign on random axis-aligned square patches inside the L_inf ball with margin-loss acceptance.
pseudocode:
1. Wrap torchattacks.Square: norm='Linf', $\epsilon$ from harness, $n_{\text{queries}} = n_q$, $p_{\text{init}} = 0.8$, loss='margin', resc_schedule=True
2. Initialize $x_{\text{adv}} = x + \epsilon \cdot \text{vertical-stripes}$
3. for $t = 1 \ldots n_q$ do
4.   Schedule patch fraction $p_t$ from $p_{\text{init}}$
5.   Pick a random square of side $h_t = \sqrt{p_t \cdot d}$ at a random position; assign each channel $\pm \epsilon$
6.   Project to $L_\infty$ ball + $[0,1]$; query margin loss; accept if margin improves
7. end for; return $x_{\text{adv}}$
diff_from_baseline: Andriushchenko, Croce, Flammarion & Hein 2020 (Square Attack, ECCV). State-of-the-art score-based $L_\infty$ attack: random sign-flip on contiguous square regions with margin-loss acceptance and a decreasing patch-size schedule.
